episodes.function: Hook the precursor problem through Nika/Jana, prove both utility and causal danger, then bring Smith/OES into a case local authority already owns.
episodes.source_span_working: early locked chapters through Smith arrival / initial OES case entry
beats: Ordinary storm dispatch establishes Nika, Jana, workload and Koren Valley before anomaly terminology.
Malformed 112 call reports a grey-van crash at Upper Gorge with precise casualty detail and four-impact background clue.
Bounded check finds no crash; evidence is preserved rather than labeled prophecy or hoax.
Eighty-five minutes later the grey van crashes; injury details and drainage-flap sound match.
Second warning names Bus 17; Jana authorizes only reversible hold-and-inspect action.
Hidden void is found and road edge collapses after bus rerouting; warning appears useful but its predicted scene no longer occurs.
Confidence pressure grows inside the rescue system.
Third warning positions volunteer Unit Four near a later real incident.
Early arrival helps free a civilian, proving real operational benefit.
Secondary rockfall kills Luka Petric while Unit Four is still exposed; intervention has a human cost.
The case stops being a puzzle and becomes a command-safety problem.
Legacy OES signature is triggered.
Smith is assigned/arrives as evidence specialist, with local operational authority explicitly remaining local.
Episode closes on the new question: not whether the calls know something, but how to use information that changes the system acting on it.
episodes.episode_change: An anomaly that could be treated as isolated evidence becomes a system-level rescue threat; Smith enters after local competence and cost are established.
episodes.emotional_wait: Can they use the next warning without creating the next casualty?

episodes.function: Break Smith’s initial suppression certainty by forcing both a suppression-linked loss and an unauthorized disclosure that may save a life, then prove response-coupling.
episodes.source_span_working: Smith investigation through dummy-response midpoint proof
beats: Smith reconstructs each warning beside the operational response it triggered; he refuses to treat prediction and action as separate logs.
OES precursor doctrine favors quarantining full content and verifying hazards independently.
A warning names road supervisor Davor Klemenc before a Lower Gorge inspection.
Present evidence supports modifying rather than cancelling the work; the culvert fails and Davor dies.
Smith cannot prove his rule killed Davor and refuses to erase the rule from the causal chain.
A later warning names Tina Vidmar and a flooding route.
Nika breaches temporary procedure and gives part of the warning to Andrej Kosir.
Andrej independently chooses an upper approach, finds Tina and gets her clear before conditions change.
The disclosure is unauthorized but materially changes the rescue path and may have saved her.
Jana forces the real question: neither obey nor suppress is sufficient as a universal rule.
A tightly bounded Confederation advisory contact supplies a response-coupled phenomenon model but no Earth authority.
The team creates an ethically bounded dummy response identifier/architecture that cannot endanger live crews.
New precursor content contains the dummy element.
Midpoint: response architecture is demonstrably part of what the warning can contain.
Smith withdraws pure suppression as sufficient and opens the deeper OES archive.
episodes.episode_change: The external-prophecy model fails; Smith’s doctrine becomes part of the mystery rather than its solution.
episodes.emotional_wait: What did OES learn before, and what did it remove from the story it tells itself?

episodes.function: Expose OES institutional memory failure, eliminate the fantasy of one correct future, and force Smith/Jana toward distributed response as the real storm arrives.
episodes.source_span_working: Morgen Pass reveal through relay/failover commitment
beats: Smith reconstructs Morgen Pass and finds the missing human decision interval behind OES suppression doctrine.
The old rule is shown to have had a real success and a real concealed cost; OES is neither vindicated nor reduced to villainy.
Smith gives Jana the causal fact she needs despite institutional resistance, sacrificing secrecy advantage before asking for trust.
Taren’s broader model is useful but shown to underweight institutional memory and the rescue cost of over-optimization.
Two legitimate response architectures are held against identical present evidence.
Precursor output diverges with the response plans; there is no single future that can simply be obeyed.
Independent weather/terrain evidence confirms a conventional multi-site emergency is forming anyway.
Jana allocates real resources on present evidence rather than precursor scripts.
The valley fragments; bounded local cells receive objectives, limits, resources and check-in obligations.
Communications failover pushes services through shared relay relationships; precursor packets become more complete as the response network re-centralizes.
OES and Confederation can describe different parts of the problem, but local communications specialists retain engineering ownership.
Selected relay relationships are isolated without treating the communications system as a magical on/off switch.
Normal failover begins to reconnect what was segmented, restoring the dangerous central pattern.
Remote abstraction is no longer enough; a physical/field intervention at the relay becomes necessary under worsening conditions.
Smith commits to the relay action while Jana delegates bounded objectives before central visibility degrades.
episodes.episode_change: Central predictive control is abandoned as the safety ideal at the exact moment the ordinary storm makes central certainty most tempting.
episodes.emotional_wait: Will distributed judgment save people when the strongest warning arrives—or merely hide a better route?

episodes.working_title: WHAT WE DID WITH THE WARNING
episodes.function: Pay the operational and human price, resolve the case through accountable uncertainty rather than prediction victory, then close on Smith’s ordinary life.
episodes.source_span_working: cascade / relay / Andrej rescue / aftermath / CH29
beats: The real storm produces simultaneous road, hydro, access and evacuation problems independent of precursor behavior.
Smith and local communications specialists isolate selected relay relationships while useful local emergency cells remain functioning.
Precursor coherence drops as the response system stops behaving like one centrally scripted graph; central situational awareness also gets worse.
Andrej becomes trapped at a hydro site and suffers a severe leg injury.
The strongest warning yet supplies a detailed access sequence that appears operationally valuable.
OES can read it; Confederation analysis can assess internal coherence; neither is entitled to convert it into field command.
Jana refuses to use the warning route as an order.
Local hydro and technical-rescue crews independently verify an old inspection route source-blind from current physical evidence.
They extract Andrej alive. The warning route is never used, so whether it would have been faster or safer remains unknowable.
The storm is contained through ordinary rescue plus the new bounded information architecture, not by solving precursor ontology.
Jana leads a casualty/decision accounting that includes local successes, central failures and Nika’s unauthorized disclosure without moral simplification.
Nika’s life-safety purpose and weak escalation path are documented; access can return after a revised override drill.
Smith replaces suppression-as-doctrine with an interim rule separating unverified precursor observation, response topology, lawful disclosure purpose and local command authority.
OES suspends Morgen Pass as a standalone precedent and restores its omitted branch; Confederation advisory closes without taking jurisdiction.
Precursor origin remains UNKNOWN. The case is contained rather than cosmologically solved.
Smith returns to Dublin. Existing F1 daughter relationship closes the story with the terse BIT? callback and his promise: tomorrow, before work.
episodes.episode_change: The main conflict closes: information is no longer allowed to become command merely because it is precise. Smith changes doctrine and personal behavior, and the institutions pay recorded consequences.
episodes.series_hook: After closure only: the source/origin of precursor recordings remains unknown; no new emergency is opened.

compression_laws: Do not merge Luka and Davor.
Do not remove Nika's unauthorized Tina/Andrej disclosure.
Do not move Smith before local characters establish the case unless a later scene-level test proves no loss of local agency.
Do not turn Taren into a commander or exposition oracle.
Do not make final rescue prove warning obedience or warning rejection.
Do not add a pre-resolution franchise cliffhanger.
